title: Does Heat Raise or Lower Blood Pressure? What Adults 35+ Need to Know
primaryKeyword: does heat raise or lower blood pressure
description: Heat typically lowers systolic BP by ~5–10 mmHg in healthy adults—but can spike it in those with hypertension. Learn how to stay safe this summer.
reasoning: This query is trending due to early-season heatwaves across North America and Europe, prompting adults 35+—especially those newly diagnosed with hypertension—to urgently reassess how weather affects their readings and meds. Users aren’t seeking textbook physiology; they want actionable, age-specific guidance on interpreting home BP changes during heat, adjusting routines (not meds), and recognizing danger signs like 140/90 in humid conditions.
